questions: How many NbSe2/CrBr3 devices did you fabricate and measure, and how many showed a zero-field diode effect? Your text names devices #1, #2 and #3.
Why were the others set aside, if any were?

Which ranges of field sweep amplitude, training field, temperature and current did you measure beyond the ones shown, and do Bcf and Bcb move when the sweep amplitude changes (for example ±50 mT versus ±6 T)?
What does the second-best device look like? Could device #2's Fig. 2-style sweeps and device #3's field dependence go in the main text?

How did you set the true zero of field at the sample, including the magnet's remanent field after the ±50 mT and ±6 T sweeps? Your Fig. 2(c) shows η moving from 45.3% to −35.7% between about −10 mT and 0 mT, so an offset of a few mT would shift Bcf, Bcb and the zero-field efficiency.
Did you measure a bare NbSe2 flake, or NbSe2 with a nonmagnetic spacer such as hBN under the CrBr3, with the same contacts and field sweeps?

For the zero-field-cooled state (−15.2%, Fig. 1(d)), from which temperature did you cool, and does the trained −35.7% survive warming above the NbSe2 Tc (staying below the CrBr3 ordering temperature) and cooling back in zero field?
Were the RMCD loops in the SM taken on the same flakes as the transport, and do the measured switching fields bracket the measured Bcf and Bcb?
